newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico receives bids for Merida III power plant.
newsitem.headline: Mexico receives bids for Merida III power plant.

text.p: Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) has received bids to build and operate the 440 megawatt Merida III thermoelectric power project, the agency said in a statement.
The concession is expected to be awarded by Feb 7 after the CFE reviews the offers, a CFE spokesman said on Thursday.
In a statement late on Wednesday, the government agency said each of the bids fulfilled minimum technical requirements, but it did not reveal the amount of the bids.
Construction and operation of the plant is expected to cost $450 million, the agency said.
Companies also registered with the CFE their bids for average cost they plan to charge under the contract per kilowatt per hour of electricity.

Merida III is scheduled to come on line in 2000 and be powered by natural gas. A separate tender for gas pipelines to supply the plant, in southern Yucatan state, is expected to take place shortly.

The plant's construction is part of a larger national electricity expansion program and will be the first to allow full private investment for energy generation. Transmission, distribution and sales will be under the government's exclusive control, the CFE said, although companies can supply electricity for their individual use.
